title: Strategic Planner (I) (LtCol to Maj) FMOS, DC PP&O
raw_text:
4.     MOS 0507, Strategic Planner (I) (LtCol to Maj) FMOS, DC PP&O

    a. Summary. Strategic Planners are developed through the combination of
advanced intermediate level education and a utilization tour as an
operational planner (0505). Their education and professional experience
prepare these officers to continue on as advanced planners at the service
level. Strategic Planners play a critical role in the development and
implementation of service policy. These officers drive the strategic
direction of the service by shaping force design, force development, and
force employment. Strategic Planners will primarily reside at the service
headquarters deputy commandant level; however, most Marine Expeditionary
Forces and service components will also rate one 0507 as a senior planner.
Select joint billets may be filled by a Strategic Planner based on available
inventory. 0507 billets are listed as additional skills designators and
maintained by DC PP&O and DC M&RA to ensure appropriate billets are staffed
with Strategic Planners.

    b. Prerequisites. Advanced intermediate level education (A-ILE) or
Joint Advanced Warfighting School complete.

    c. Requirements. Marine officers are awarded this MOS after 12
successful months in an 0505 billet or to the satisfaction of the commanding
officer, whichever is shorter. Requests for this FMOS will be submitted to a
servicing IPAC with an endorsement from the first general officer in the
Marine’s chain of command.

    d. Duties. Lead strategic planning efforts for the service
headquarters. Conduct complex problem solving, assist senior leader decision
making, and align service resources with national strategic guidance.

    e.      Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
None.

       f.   Related Military Skill.   None.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
